description.value: East Van Roasters is a social enterprise cafe and bean-to-bar chocolate maker in Vancouver's Downtown Eastside, providing career training and meaningful employment for women experiencing barriers to employment. The cafe serves specialty espresso drinks, single-origin drinking chocolates, and freshly baked cookies, with an open-door community ethos that includes a suspended coffee program for local community members. The business has taken home multiple International Chocolate Awards and makes all its single-origin chocolates on-site.

bike_parking_detail: 6 racks within 100m: stands (2 spaces) at 19m; stands (6 spaces) at 30m; stands (6 spaces) at 39m; stands at 44m; stands (2 spaces) at 79m; stands (4 spaces) at 94m. Total: 20 spaces.

enrichment_extras.reasoning: The website fully corroborates the OSM address (319 Carrall Street, V6B 2J4) and phone number (604-629-7562). The community FAQ page explicitly states an open washroom policy, confirming washrooms are available to visitors. The menu page confirms vegan alternatives for all drinks; no evidence was found for bike parking, Wi-Fi, water refill, or most other cycling amenities anywhere in the website content.
concerns: The website displays two conflicting sets of operating hours within the same pages: one block shows Tuesday–Friday only (closed Saturday, Sunday, Monday), while a second block shows Monday–Saturday; OSM tags list Tuesday–Saturday. It is unclear which hours are current and accurate.
A second East Van Roasters location at 16 W Hastings St, Vancouver, V6B 1G4 (phone: 604-336-3528) is listed on the website and may warrant a separate OSM record check to avoid duplication.
enrichment_extras.recommended_status_reason: A well-established, award-winning social enterprise cafe with confirmed washrooms, vegan options, and a welcoming community ethos; a worthwhile and distinctive stop for touring cyclists in the Downtown Eastside.
enrichment_extras.notes: The website's suspended coffee program and overdose-alert bathroom device reflect a highly community-oriented operation; these are not cycling amenities but do speak to the welcoming and accessible character of the venue.

Washrooms.detail: Community FAQ page states: 'We have an open washroom policy (for going to the bathroom and maybe a bird bath) not for a safe injection site.'
